hints: Resolve the 12 N applied force horizontally along the smooth floor: $F_x = 12\cos 25^\circ$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $F_x = ma \implies 12\cos 25^\circ = 3a$.
Solve for the acceleration: $a = 4\cos 25^\circ \approx 3.625\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use the constant-acceleration formula $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ and $t = 5\text{ s}$ to calculate the distance.
walkthrough:
Resolve the applied force horizontally along the smooth floor to determine the net accelerating force:
$$F_x = 12\cos 25^\circ \approx 10.8757\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally to find the acceleration $a$ of the $3\text{ kg}$ block:
$$F_x = ma \implies 12\cos 25^\circ = 3a$$
$$a = 4\cos 25^\circ \approx 3.6252\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply the SUVAT equation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ from rest ($u = 0$) for $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$s = 0(5) + \frac{1}{2}(4\cos 25^\circ)(5^2) = 2(25)\cos 25^\circ = 50\cos 25^\circ$$
$$s \approx 50 \times 0.906308 \approx 45.3154\text{ m} \approx 45.3\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State Newton's second law along the horizontal direction:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$

The floor is smooth, so there is no friction. The only horizontal force is the horizontal component of the $12\text{ N}$ force:
$$F_x = 12\cos 25^\circ$$

Substitute $F_x$ and mass $m = 3\text{ kg}$ into Newton's second law:
$$12\cos 25^\circ = 3a$$

Divide both sides by $3$ to isolate acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{12\cos 25^\circ}{3} = 4\cos 25^\circ \approx 4 \times 0.906308 = 3.62523\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

State the SUVAT formula for displacement under uniform acceleration:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$

Substitute $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (initially at rest), $a = 4\cos 25^\circ$, and $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$s = 0 \times 5 + \frac{1}{2} \times (4\cos 25^\circ) \times 5^2$$
$$s = 2\cos 25^\circ \times 25 = 50\cos 25^\circ$$

Compute the distance to 3 significant figures:
$$s = 50 \times 0.906308 \approx 45.3154\text{ m} = 45.3\text{ m} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
